calls.head: Tired legs for the Mammoth
calls.body: The Mammoth played last night and get no rest before this one. Teams in that spot usually get the worse of the chances, so we expect the Blues to control more of the play than they usually do.

calls.head: Don’t buy Vejmelka’s slump against the Blues
calls.body: Vejmelka has been shaky against the Blues since 2023-24, well below his usual. But three seasons of data say a goalie’s record against one team tells us nothing about the next meeting, so don’t be surprised if he looks like himself tonight.

UTA.head: We leaned Utah’s way (59%), but St. Louis had other ideas.

STL.head: We had St. Louis as slight underdogs (41%), and they pulled it off.

surprises.head: Joel Hofer stole one
surprises.body: Hofer stopped all 29 shots, worth 3.3 expected goals, through overtime. That is more than St. Louis’s winning margin. Starting goalies have a night this good about once every 100 starts. Most starters don’t get one a season.

surprises.head: Utah shortened their bench
surprises.body: Utah leans on their bottom six more than most teams. Not tonight: the bottom six played 36% of the forwards’ 5-on-5 time, against their usual 44% and a league average of 42%. A team strays this far about once every 200 games. That’s rarer than once a season for any one team.

story.head: Hofer blanks the Mammoth
paras: No goal counted through overtime. Liam O'Brien and Ross Johnston squared off early in the first. St. Louis had a goal taken off for offside midway through the second, though it didn’t end up costing them. The shootout went eight rounds, and Connor McMichael won it for the Blues after Jake Neighbours and Jimmy Snuggerud had scored earlier.
The Mammoth had a little more of the play, but the Blues had the finish. Joel Hofer stopped all 29 shots for the Blues, and Karel Vejmelka kept the Mammoth in it, stopping 22 of 22.

Neither power play scored: the Blues killed all four Mammoth power plays, and the Mammoth killed all five of St. Louis’. The Blues improved to 9-8-2, seventh in the Central, while the Mammoth dropped to 10-8-2, fifth in the Central.
